clue.text: Look good, heading for crag with agile mountaineer

parts.note: to rock an outfit is, informally, to look good in it

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the start of crag is used

parts.note: limber means supple or agile

explanation.surface: Praise for a nimble climber who looks the part on the crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look good' is the slang verb ROCK, as in 'you rock that jacket'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who scales rock faces is a mountaineer of a kind.

clue.text: Upset and mostly irritable following a guide

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: ratty is British slang for irritable
someone following a guide is led along

explanation.surface: A tourist trailing behind a guide grows cross and edgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following a guide' is not a placement signal: whoever follows a guide is LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be thrown off balance emotionally is to be upset.

clue.text: Easily-retained energy abstracted from college in island

indicators.note: in places the shortened college inside the island word

parts.note: a cay is a small low island

indicators.note: abstracted means taken away, so energy's letter leaves the college word

parts.note: a tech is a technical college
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy drained from a college on an island, with an odd hyphenated adjective about memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstracted from' removes energy's letter from the college; 'in' sets what is left inside the island. A tune easily retained is catchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is easily retained in the memory is described as catchy.

clue.text: Half-hearted policeman, copper in the wrong, upset old scientist

indicators.note: the heart of the policeman word is its central pair of letters, and half of that pair goes

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: in puts copper's symbol inside the reversed wrong
upset in a down clue turns the word for wrong backwards

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A dispirited bent policeman troubles an old scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' removes one of the two middle letters of the policeman; 'upset' reverses the wrong, and 'in' puts copper's symbol inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Copernicus was the Renaissance astronomer who placed the sun at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: Jack dropped in an instant, being dodgy

indicators.note: dropped means the letter for jack is let fall from the word

parts.note: a jiffy is an instant
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack quickly dropped, for shady reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something doubtful or of questionable quality is dodgy.

clue.text: Substantial obscurity surrounding a criminal union member

indicators.note: surrounding means the two words go round the letter a

parts.note: substantial means big
mist is a cause of obscurity

explanation.surface: A shadowy figure wraps round a criminal trade unionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is marriage, and the crime is having two spouses at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with two spouses at once commits the crime of bigamy within the union of marriage.

clue.text: Always keeping wordless singing up? It's the booze

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole is read from bottom to top
keeping means the always word holds the singing

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
la-la is singing without words

explanation.surface: Pub-goers forever singing la-la-la, blamed on the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER holding LALA gives ELALAER, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is a traditionally brewed British beer, so it is booze.

clue.text: Matches leader in support for race

parts.note: to pit one against another is to match them
the top is the leader

explanation.surface: A frontrunner backs a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: During a motor race, cars halt briefly for refuelling and new tyres: race support.

clue.text: Dig north, going under flat areas, not mincing words

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under puts the dig and north below the flat areas

parts.note: plains are flat areas
a dig is a poke

explanation.surface: An instruction to dig north beneath flat ground, said bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frank and blunt in speech does not mince words.

clue.text: Vehicle light with flash installed by dude

indicators.note: installed by means the flash word is set inside the dude word

parts.note: a fop or dandy is a dude
flash and glam both mean showy

explanation.surface: A dandy fits a car light with a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright lamp fitted to a car for driving in poor visibility is a vehicle light.

clue.text: Broken carpal tests its treatment?

indicators.note: broken means the letters of carpal tests are smashed and reset

explanation.surface: Wrist bones that fail their tests get the obvious remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the letters of 'carpal tests' are reshuffled, and a broken carpal (wrist bone) is treated in a cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fractured wrist is set in a rigid plaster mould, the standard treatment.

clue.text: Missing a froth in beer is perfectly rational

indicators.note: in places the shortened froth inside the beer word

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: missing means the a is left out of froth's word

parts.note: lather is froth

explanation.surface: A beer with no head is somehow quite sane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' drops the A from froth's word, and 'in' sets the remainder inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who is fully sane and alert mentally is described as all there.

clue.text: The writer's friend — a beastly bounder

parts.note: the writer is the setter speaking, so the writer's (writer is) gives I'm
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An author introduces a pal who is a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like an old word for a cad, but here it is an animal that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope famous for leaping, a literal bounding animal.

clue.text: Mischievous character sent up church telegram without error

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous character

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue reverses the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a cable is a telegram

explanation.surface: An imp mocks the church by sending a telegram, and no mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless conduct or work is impeccable, without any error.

clue.text: Prompt in shedding last of clothing?

definitions.text: Prompt in shedding last of clothing?

indicators.note: shedding means the final letter of clothing is cast off from prompt's word

parts.note: to nudge is to prompt

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of clothing

explanation.surface: An undresser is urged to drop the final garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes someone who has shed the last item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has taken off every last piece of clothing is unclothed and bare.

clue.text: It has to — in case holding that is seen as an indication

definitions.text: that is seen as an indication

indicators.note: holding means the in case word wraps round the others

parts.note: lest means in case
must means has to

explanation.surface: An instruction about what a container must hold, read as a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive indicator of quality or opinion is a litmus test, from the chemical indicator paper.

clue.text: Huge failure, investing in fuel

indicators.note: investing in means failure goes inside fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a loss is a failure

explanation.surface: An enormous flop after putting money into fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something gigantic in size is colossal.

clue.text: Key worker's reputation suffering? Not initially for a time

indicators.note: suffering means the letters of reputation are knocked about
for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of not

explanation.surface: An essential worker's good name takes a battering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially for a time' swaps one T of REPUTATION for N, then 'suffering' rearranges the result. 'Key worker' sounds like an essential employee, but means someone who works on piano keys.
explanation.definitionFit: This person adjusts the keys and strings of a piano, so works on keys.

clue.text: Is rousing funeral party interrupting a couple of Poles?

indicators.note: interrupting means the funeral party breaks into a and the poles

parts.note: N and S are the North and South poles
a wake is a gathering after a funeral

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a noisy funeral gathering among two Polish guests stirs anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the North and South poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-person verb: someone who is rousing from sleep awakens.

clue.text: Obscure comments by publisher left unfinished

indicators.note: left unfinished means the last letter of the publisher's comments is dropped

parts.note: a blurb is the publisher's promotional comment on a book

explanation.surface: A publisher's remarks trail off, leaving things murky.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to make indistinct or hazy is to blur.

clue.text: Light working with nothing plugged in? It must be a spoof

parts.note: a lamp is a light

indicators.note: plugged in means nothing is put inside working

parts.note: on means working
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lamp switched on with nothing plugged in must be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugged in' looks like electrics, but puts O inside ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a satirical mocking imitation is a spoof.

clue.text: Promises of reimbursement after party turned nasty

indicators.note: after means the IOUs come behind the party
turned means the party word is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
IOUs are written promises to repay

explanation.surface: After a party, unpaid IOUs make things turn ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hateful and repugnant things are odious, nasty.

clue.text: Film star required for take at once

indicators.note: the letters required are contained in the run of words take at once

explanation.surface: A movie star is needed on set for an immediate take.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton (or Diane Keaton) is a famous film star.

clue.text: Learned people targeted accountant in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: aimed means targeted
ACA is an Associate Chartered Accountant

explanation.surface: Scholars targeted an accountant during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' suggests economics, but means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The world of universities and scholars is collectively academia, the learned people.

clue.text: Resent man with message leaving fourth item out

indicators.note: leaving out means a letter is omitted from the messenger word
out completes leaving out, signalling omission

parts.note: an envoy is a man carrying a message
O is the fourth letter of the messenger word

explanation.surface: Resentment at a messenger who left out the fourth point.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to begrudge someone what they have is to resent them.

clue.text: Name otherwise adopted by fashionable composer

indicators.note: adopted by means otherwise is taken inside fashionable

parts.note: in means fashionable
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: A trendy composer goes by a different name.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of symphonies.

clue.text: Bash that's underhand in fight

indicators.note: in puts underhand inside the fight word

parts.note: a bout is a fight
low means underhand or mean

explanation.surface: A party with dirty tactics during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a blow, but is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A big lavish party or feast is a blowout, informally a bash.

clue.text: Lightweight journalism delivered by one ass?

definitions.text: Lightweight journalism delivered by one ass?

parts.words: Lightweight journalism delivered by one ass?
parts.note: the summer slack period brings trivial news; read cryptically, what a silly creature delivers is a son, its offspring

explanation.surface: Trivial news coverage written by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The summer lull when papers run trivial stories; read differently, an ass (a silly) delivering 'a son' gives silly's a son.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet summer months when newspapers print frivolous filler stories have this name.
